title: B'Tselem Report 'The Elimination Project' Accuses Israel of Systematic Campaign to Erase Palestinian Presence in West Bank
detail: The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem published a report on Monday, September 14, 2026, titled 'The Elimination Project,' arguing that Israeli policy in the occupied West Bank amounts to a systematic dismantling of the conditions that allow Palestinians to function as a community, rather than a series of isolated incidents. Drawing on roughly 2,000 Palestinian testimonies, the report identifies five interconnected mechanisms: violence and intimidation by military forces and armed settler militias; movement restrictions (925 physical obstacles -- gates and checkpoints -- recorded by December 2025); economic strangulation (West Bank unemployment doubling to 27.5% by end-2025, 115,000 work permits frozen); social and political destruction; and what the report calls ethnic cleansing. It says settlers now control nearly 20% of West Bank territory, records 1,600+ settler attacks in 2025, 104 new settlements approved since 2022, and at least 1,107 Palestinians killed by Israeli forces in the West Bank between October 2023 and the report's publication. The report links the current campaign to a 2017 'Decisive Plan' and says the pace has accelerated since October 2023. The Israeli government did not immediately respond to the report's characterization.

title: Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zohar Vows to Revoke Citizenship of 'NAZA' Documentary Filmmakers Over 'Treason'
detail: Israeli Culture and Sport Minister Miki Zohar said on Monday, September 14, 2026 that he would move to revoke the Israeli citizenship of 'NAZA' filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, days after their documentary on the IDF's 'Lavender' AI targeting system received a record-length ovation at its Venice Film Festival premiere and won the festival's Special Jury Prize. Zohar called the film 'vile' and accused the directors of damaging Israel's image 'just to get applause from antisemites around the world,' describing their actions as 'treason against the state.' Under Israeli law, a minister has no unilateral power to strip citizenship; revocation on disloyalty grounds requires a formal process involving the interior minister and the courts, which had not been initiated at time of reporting. Other Israeli officials, including former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, had separately denounced the film as a 'blood libel.'
